sections.What we use it for:
Files under `template/` and `.schema/` cite the documentation site by URL, and every corpus that took the framework keeps a copy of them. A page that moves would break each of those links in every such corpus, and no check here reads an external URL. The plugin keeps each old URL working.

`redirect_maps` in `mkdocs.yml` lists each moved page and the page that replaced it. The page it writes keeps the
anchor. `NavigationTests` in `kac.tests` fails a redirect whose target the nav does not list.
sections.Status:
The approval stops at 1.2.2, because the ProperDocs project publishes every release from 1.2.3. PyPI names
`ProperDocs/mkdocs-redirects` as the publisher of 1.2.3, and that release requires `properdocs`, a fork of MkDocs with
no record here. Release 1.2.3 changes nothing in how a redirect is built. [Issue #1058] decides which toolchain the site
follows.
sections.Licence and obligations: MIT. It asks that the copyright notice travel with a copy of the software. The site is generated output and not a copy of the plugin, so nothing follows for what is published.
